observation_summary: The method getResult() in MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer was returning the result of the last optimizer run rather than the best result found across all starts, leading to incorrect values in tests.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the return value of the methods getResult() and getFunctionValue() to point to the first element of the sorted optima/optimaValues arrays (optima[0] and optimaValues[0]) instead of delegating to the underlying optimizer's last result. This is a correction of an incorrect value assignment/retrieval logic, fitting the Assignment/Initialization category.
evidence_used: The bug report states that getResult() returns the result of the last run, which is not necessarily the best one.
The fix diff shows changing 'return optimizer.getResult();' to 'return optima[0];' and 'return optimizer.getFunctionValue();' to 'return optimaValues[0];'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While this involves a method, the core issue is that the method was returning the wrong piece of data (the last result instead of the best result), which is a classic case of incorrect value assignment/retrieval rather than a flaw in the computational algorithm itself.
